analysis.title: Markets On The Move - Asia Equity Flows Mixed; NZD Front-End Option Supply Emerges
key_insights: Japan semiconductor and electronic components names led the selloff (Taiyo Yuden -12%, Kioxia -12%, Murata -10%) as early US midterm results pointed to a Democratic sweep, which the desk says triggered a sharp unwind of the Trump/AI trade. Japan flows are 62% better to buy.

Taiwan flows are 59% sellers. TAIEX turned early gains into losses of over 1300 points and was testing 42K. AI names kept selling off and margin calls are a risk, with many names below the 130% threshold.

Korea saw foreign cash net outflows of $1.6bn, mostly taken by retail investors. National Pension had sold only $52mn. Nasdaq futures were down 2.2%, with pro-Trump sectors like AI leading the region lower.
Hong Kong/China flows are 52% to buy with 3% in shorts. The desk is buying healthcare, consumer and technology and selling financials.

ASEAN flows are 59% better to sell, most active in Singapore. India is buy skewed with inflows into FMCG, capital markets, healthcare, banks, two-wheelers and telecoms. Australia flows are 59% sell skewed, concentrated in industrials, utilities and basic materials.
New Zealand's weak jobs data make the Nov. 7 election more interesting. The market priced a gap move in the OCR from the 60bp handle to over 70bp over the past week.

NZD risk reversals are likely to be better bid for puts, and more hikes would get priced out if Labour wins, because an employment objective would be added back to the RBNZ mandate. Front-end option supply has been emerging, with 1w1m NZD and 1w1m AUDNZD looking stretched.
